clue.text: Like Byron's swimming feat? More like his predecessor's

definitions.meaning: Byron swam the Hellespont in 1810, a brave and celebrated exploit
the legendary Leander swam the same strait nightly to reach his lover, the priestess Hero

explanation.surface: A literary aside comparing Byron's famous swim with that of the mythical lover who swam it first.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander, in Greek myth, swam the Hellespont each night to visit Hero; Byron repeated the swim. So the second reading splits the answer as HERO + IC, 'belonging to Hero'.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's crossing was a bold, admirable exploit, and the second sense ties the swim to Leander's beloved by name.

clue.text: Start with Cicero

parts.note: reads as an instruction to begin by reading Cicero, but means the opening part of an oration in classical rhetoric

explanation.walkthrough: In Latin rhetoric, of which Cicero was master, a speech opens with its introductory section; the clue names that opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical orators began with an introductory section to win the audience, the speech's beginning.

clue.text: Unqualified ambition of the leftists

definitions.meaning: the left wing wants the right wing out of power

explanation.surface: Left-wing politicians nurse a goal with no reservations.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: what the left wants is the political right out.
explanation.definitionFit: A total, absolute victory has no conditions attached, and the left wing wants its rivals ousted.

clue.text: E.g. he manufactures this kind of butter

definitions.text: E.g. he manufactures this kind of butter

parts.words: E.g. he manufactures this kind of butter
parts.note: the letters of 'E.g. he' can be made into ghee, the Indian butter that has been melted and strained

explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the letters E, G, H, E gives GHEE, and ghee is butter of the strained kind, so the clue defines the type of butter by spelling its example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is butter heated to separate and remove its milk solids, leaving pure clear fat.

clue.text: "Hair " out of step?-is it a sin?

indicators.note: the word for hair is built out of, i.e. wrapped round, the dance step placed in its middle

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
pas is the French-derived ballet word for a dance step

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether hair that is out of step with fashion counts as a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of step' looks like one phrase, but 'out of' is the container signal and 'step' is the ballet word on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Lord's Prayer, 'forgive us our trespasses' uses the word for wrongs or sins against others.

clue.text: But it's not so much angular as rounded of course

definitions.text: But it's not so much angular as rounded of course

parts.words: But it's not so much angular as rounded of course
parts.note: a famous bend that horses round on the Epsom Derby course, so it is a corner that is rounded rather than angular

explanation.walkthrough: Tattenham Corner is the sweeping bend on Epsom Downs racecourse where the Derby is run; 'of course' means on a racecourse, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby field races round this curve at Epsom, so it is a turn on a racecourse rather than a sharp angle.

clue.text: The Lizard has a sun and air development

indicators.note: the letters undergo development into a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cornwall's Lizard peninsula enjoys sunshine and fresh breezes as it is developed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard is a Cornish peninsula, but here it is the animal. 'Development' rearranges A SUN and AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Saurian is the zoological adjective and noun for lizards and related reptiles.

clue.text: 'eavenly music, the food I love

parts.note: the harp is the instrument of heaven; the dropped H of 'eavenly tells you to drop it from harp too
an egg is a food
love is nil in tennis, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A cockney rhapsodises about heavenly music and the food he adores.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eavenly shows a dropped H, and the harp of heaven loses its H the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a chord played as a run of separate notes, as on a harp.

clue.text: Weekend, day off, organize tea, get soaked

indicators.note: the day is taken off the weekend day, removed from its end

parts.note: Saturday is one day of the weekend
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of tea are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A to-do list for a weekend day off: make the tea and get drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' removes DAY from SATURDAY, leaving SATUR; 'organize' turns TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak something completely, so the verb is a synonym for drenching.

clue.text: Painted lady for instance

parts.note: a painted lady is a butterfly, but read literally it is a woman captured on canvas by a painter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the butterfly called a painted lady; the clue really means a lady who has been painted, a picture of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of a woman is an example of a likeness of a person on canvas.

clue.text: That one with the waggly tail — not self-motivated ?

definitions.text: That one with the waggly tail
definitions.meaning: a young dog kept as a pet wags its tail
a marionette moves only when someone works its strings

explanation.surface: A description of a wagging dog that lacks any drive of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into a young dog and a pet animal; the second is the string-worked doll, which never moves of its own accord.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is worked by another's hand, and a young dog kept at home is a pup that is a pet.

clue.text: A learned cleric has it, and I have that something extra

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a highly educated clergyman
taken as written
've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: A scholarly priest has something, and the speaker claims to have a little extra too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' and 'and' are link words; the pieces run A, DD, IT, I, VE in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is a substance put into food or fuel on top of its basic ingredients.

clue.text: Dancing club ?

parts.note: read as a society for dancers, but meant as a golf club whose name sounds like one who dances a jig

explanation.walkthrough: A jigger is an old type of golf iron; the name also reads as 'one who jigs', so the club itself is the dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: The jigger is a golfing iron, and a jig is a lively dance, so the word joins dancing and club.

clue.text: Increase the number in the layer

indicators.note: the number is placed in the layer, so the bird's word wraps round it

parts.note: a hen lays eggs, so in crosswords it is a layer
eight is one example of a number

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise the head count in a stratum of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' suggests a stratum or sheet, but in crosswords it is the egg-laying bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something, make it greater or more intense, is a synonym of increasing it.

clue.text: When seats are empty but there's standing room only

definitions.text: When seats are empty but there's standing room only

parts.words: When seats are empty but there's standing room only
parts.note: reads like a theatre with empty seats yet full standing room, but means vacant parliamentary seats with candidates standing for them

explanation.walkthrough: Parliamentary seats fall vacant and candidates 'stand' for them, so standing is the only way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Polls are held to fill vacant seats in a legislature, with candidates standing for office.

clue.text: Be exclusive!

parts.note: reads as advice to be select and snobbish, but means exclude something, leave it out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' suggests a smart club; here it means excluding, which is what leaving out does.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to exclude it, the literal sense of acting exclusively.

clue.text: Get artist's cramp with pencil? Change into red ink

definitions.meaning: draw too much and the hand cramps
take out more than the account holds, so the balance goes into the red

explanation.surface: An artist overworks his pencil hand, then turns to red ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank statements once printed debts in red ink, so going into the red means owing the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching to excess, and withdrawing more money than the account holds, putting it in debit.

clue.text: But not the way to jug your hare

definitions.text: But not the way to jug your hare

parts.words: But not the way to jug your hare
parts.note: to jug a hare is to stew it, but jug is also slang for jail

explanation.walkthrough: Jugged hare is hare stewed in a pot; 'jug' is also slang for putting someone in prison, which is not how you cook a hare.
explanation.definitionFit: Jug is slang for jail, so the sense meant is to lock up.

clue.text: Evelyn, Anthony, of diamond fame

parts.note: three namesakes: the girl in Browning's poem 'Evelyn ...', the novelist Anthony ... who wrote The Prisoner of Zenda, and the famous blue diamond

explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists three famous bearers of one surname: Browning's poem title, the author Anthony, and the large blue diamond in the Smithsonian.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname links a Browning poem's heroine, a Victorian novelist and a legendary gem.

clue.text: Such is the seal of the thrice greatest

definitions.text: Such is the seal of the thrice greatest

parts.words: Such is the seal of the thrice greatest
parts.note: Hermes Trismegistus, 'thrice greatest', was the legendary father of alchemy, credited with the airtight seal

explanation.walkthrough: An airtight seal is named after Hermes Trismegistus ('thrice greatest'), the mythical founder of alchemy.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight closure takes its name from the legendary alchemist Hermes Trismegistus.

clue.text: Showed earlier partiality, the chairman did

definitions.meaning: a chairman was in the chair, conducting a meeting

explanation.surface: The meeting's chairman is accused of having taken sides from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as 'pre-sided', took sides beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman chairs a meeting, and taking sides beforehand is the split reading.

clue.text: Carpenter booked for getting a lady out of bed

indicators.note: the lady is getting out of the bed, so the bed sits within her letters

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tradesman is arrested for helping a woman out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Bede, hero of George Eliot's novel, is a carpenter; 'booked' says he lives in a book, not that he was arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of George Eliot's 1859 novel works as a carpenter, so he is a carpenter in a book.

clue.text: Belgian queen going East-on horseback ?.

parts.note: Astrid was Queen of the Belgians, wife of Leopold III
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Belgium's queen heads east riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Astrid of Belgium (died 1935) was the wife of King Leopold III; 'going' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits with one leg on each side of the horse, so mounted with legs apart.

clue.text: " Alas ! for the — Of Christian charity" (Hood)

definitions.text: " Alas ! for the — Of Christian charity" (Hood)

parts.words: " Alas ! for the — Of Christian charity" (Hood)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Thomas Hood's poem The Bridge of Sighs

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood's The Bridge of Sighs laments that kindness to the drowned girl is scarce; the missing word rhymes with 'charity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood says Christian charity is uncommon, a scarce thing, which fills the gap.

clue.text: One of the revue company, full of 17 ac

definitions.meaning: a member of The Co-..., a popular 1920s concert party revue
17 across is the word for expectation, so this means brimming with that feeling

explanation.surface: A cheerful member of a variety troupe brims with expectation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-Optimists were a famous British revue troupe of the 1920s, so a member was one of the optimists in the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sure that things will turn out well is brimming with confidence about the future.

clue.text: John's College, Oxford

parts.note: reads like St John's College, but names John the Victorian critic and the Oxford college named after him

explanation.walkthrough: St John's is an Oxford college, which is the false trail; the clue means the college in Oxford that bears the critic John's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian art critic John gave his surname to an Oxford college for working people founded in 1899.

clue.text: M, A or P, Anglice

parts.note: in the abbreviations a.m. and p.m. the M stands for the Latin meridiem, midday; Anglice means 'in English'

explanation.walkthrough: A.M. and P.M. are ante and post meridiem; the M is midday, given here in plain English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin meridiem in a.m. and p.m. means midday, the middle of the day in English.

clue.text: Aimless traveller in difficulty drew near

indicators.note: letters in difficulty are in disorder, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller with no aim gets into trouble as he approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In difficulty' rearranges DREW NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover who drifts from place to place without a fixed goal roams freely.

clue.text: See about the end-of-year return and withdraw

indicators.note: the word see goes about, i.e. around, the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the month's short form is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: December, the year's last month, is abbreviated Dec

explanation.surface: Look over the year-end tax return, then pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a tax return filed at year's end, but it signals the month's short form read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to formally leave a federation or union, to pull out of it.
